item.text:
<linkedin_post>Dartmouth Provost Santiago Schnell resigned after a faculty committee found that he had used AI to meaningfully alter his writing and was not forthcoming about it. Among the pieces examined was his Washington Post column about AI cheating in universities.

Schnell said the column was based on his own thinking and that he used ChatGPT to refine arguments. His account and the committee’s finding show why broad terms like “AI-assisted” leave room for different interpretations.

A university could make its expectations clearer by asking writers to describe what they used a tool for: correcting language, reorganizing a draft or developing arguments. That would give readers a better account of how the work was produced than a simple statement that AI was used.</linkedin_post>
